newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU ministers agree long-distance call system.
newsitem.headline: EU ministers agree long-distance call system.

text.p: European Union telecommunications ministers agreed on Friday to introduce a system to make it easier for phone companies to compete for long-distance and international calls.

Known as "carrier pre-selection", it will allow consumers who want to make long-distance calls to choose competitors to the traditional phone monopolies without having to dial a special code -- a system already used in the United States.

The ministers agreed that most countries should introduce it by the start of 2000, two years after the EU deadline for opening telecoms markets to full competition. They asked the European Commission to draw up legislation.
But they adopted language that could allow Britain to argue against introducing it in its own market, officials said.

Britain, where cable TV companies are investing heavily in building networks that provide local phone service to compete with former monopoly British Telecommunications, is wary about carrier pre-selection.
It fears that the practice could hurt the newcomers by making it easier for consumers to bypass them when choosing a long-distance carrier.
But other EU states and the Commission argue that pre-carrier selection will promote competition by making it easier for callers to choose new market entrants as their long-distance carriers.

Some noted that British Telecom advocated the practice when operating abroad. "In other countries, British Telecom is pressing the hardest to get pre-selection on line," Dutch Public Works Minister Annemarie Jorritsma-Lebbink, who chaired the meeting, told reporters.
The ministers agreed language, however, that would allow Britain to argue that introducing the system there would not "encourage competition in all sectors of the market".
The text is not binding, however, and the formal solution will only be found once legislation is adopted.

The ministers also endorsed "number portability" -- the ability of consumers to take their numbers with them when they change phone companies -- and said countries should introduce it no later than the year 2003.

They should try to do it, however, within two years after the deadline for fully liberalising their markets. Greece, Ireland, Luxembourg, Portugal and Spain have been granted delays to the 1998 deadline that applies to most countries.
